LESSON: READING 3.2.2 COMPREHENSION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.2: Reading 3.2.2 Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 3.2.2 Comprehension, part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two General.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to understand what we read?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 3.2.2 Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital literacy: Interaction with digital devices is enhanced as the learner reads simple digital texts.

• Creativity and imagination: is enhanced as the learner makes predictions about a story.

Values:
• Unity: Cooperation is enhanced as the learner collaborates with others in groups activities.

• Respect: Acceptance as the learner appreciates diverse opinions of others during group activities.

Link to Pertinent Contemporary Issues:

Education for Sustainable Development: Disaster Risk Reduction is enhanced as the learner becomes aware of safety in the use of the

different modes of transport.

Link to other Learning areas:

Reading for comprehension is practised in all learning areas.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Digital text, assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners, adapted digital devices

with filter keys/key guards/larger mouse/head control input devices such as head wand

Other Related Service Providers: Resource person, speech therapist, Learner support assistance, Occupational Therapist, Physiotherapist.
